name: sol_am_replayattack_2
description: Cross-chain signature replay due to missing chain ID / domain separator binding
question: The source file in `source` verifies off-chain generated signatures (e.g., via ecrecover or a signature-based authorization function) to authorize an action, but the signed message or EIP-712 domain separator does not include chain ID or any other chain-specific parameter, so a valid signature produced for one chain can be replayed to authorize the same action on a different chain, excluding cases where the domain separator or signed payload already incorporates block.chainid or an equivalent unique chain identifier.
criteria: A function recovers a signer via ecrecover using a message hash built only from function arguments, a nonce, and contract address, without including chain ID
An EIP-712 domain separator is constructed with name, version, and verifyingContract but omits chainid, allowing the same signature to validate on multiple deployments
A permit-style approval function checks signature validity and nonce but never binds the signed struct to the current chain's identifier
A meta-transaction relayer verifies a user signature against a hash that excludes block.chainid, enabling replay of the same signed transaction on a forked or sibling chain
